notes.title: Design traversal routes for actual speed and turning
notes.observation: Driving tests in V6 found slaloms and tight laps that a boosted skiff could not follow, although their layouts had looked plausible. The author changed routes and measured runs with the game's boat physics.
notes.recommendation: When speed or steering changes, traverse routes at the intended speed and retest entrances, turns, braking, and exits. Validate human feel separately from autopilot completion.
applies_when: Creating movement courses
Increasing player or vehicle speed
limits: Skiff turning radii are game-specific tuning
Autopilot success is not proof that a beginner enjoys or understands the route

evidence.detail: Sections 2, 3, 12, and 13 describe measured driving failures, repairs, and remaining human tests.

notes.title: Check a test route's water depth before treating a stopped chaser as a bug
notes.observation: A sea monster stopped chasing a scripted boat after one bite. The scripted route crossed an island's shallows, where the monster is designed to stop; the boat also ran aground there. Scanning candidate routes with downward raycasts first (water surface to seabed along the heading) and driving the deep one showed four bites in 30 seconds and no stop.
notes.recommendation: Before judging an AI chase from a scripted drive, verify the route stays in conditions the AI is meant to follow into (depth, zones), and log the AI's own state over time alongside the target's.
applies_when: Testing pursuers with scripted or autopilot movement
limits: One game's Leviathan and route; Studio, one client

evidence.detail: Point 6 (the Leviathan): four bites in 30 s on a deep route.
V13.1 lessons (4) in the game description.

notes.title: A script source of 200,000 characters or more cannot be set, so split generated data
notes.observation: An exporter wrote one Luau module per asset holding its mesh arrays; one came out at 592,318 characters. Setting it as a ModuleScript's Source from a Studio plugin context failed with 'Provided string length (592318) is greater than or equal to max length (200000)'; Rojo's live sync sets sources the same way. Writing one module per material group, and cutting groups over 2,200 triangles, kept every module under 165,000 characters.
notes.recommendation: Make any generator that writes Luau data assert each file's length is under 200,000 characters and split by a natural unit (a group, a chunk) when it is not; check the largest file in tests.
applies_when: Generating Luau modules from tools (meshes, layouts, tables of data) that are synced by Rojo or a plugin
limits: A Rojo build to a place file was not tested with an oversized module

evidence.detail: Sections 1 and 9: the 590,000-character module and the split.

notes.title: Moving a character out of a seat from the server can be undone by its client
notes.observation: At a round's end the server destroyed a driver's SeatWeld and set their root's CFrame to a spawn on a ship. A trace showed them on the ship for one sample, then back beside the boat a fifth of a second later: their own client, which owned the character's physics, still held them in the seat and its position replicated back. Retrying the move for up to two seconds whenever the character was found far from the spawn fixed it.
notes.recommendation: After moving a character that was seated or otherwise client-owned a moment before, verify a few frames later that the move took and repeat it if not, instead of assuming one CFrame write is final.
applies_when: Respawning, round resets or teleports of players who may be in vehicle seats
Client-owned character physics
limits: Observed in Studio with zero network latency on one client; real latency may make it more frequent
Only VehicleSeat-style seats were tested

evidence.detail: Bug 9 in section 19: before the fix the goblin was aboard at +0.3 s and back at sea at +0.5 s; after it, aboard for the whole 8 s checked.

notes.title: Let a player play on a stand-in profile while another server still holds their save
notes.observation: Profiles were opened and saved with one UpdateAsync that checks a session lock. In a Studio test with an in-memory store, a fresh lock planted by 'another server' made this server refuse to open the profile; after five tries (16 s) the player kept playing on a blank stand-in, earned 18 Shinies from a raid while purchases were refused, and the stored profile stayed untouched. When the other lock was released, a background retry opened the real profile within 20 s and added the earnings (525 + 18 = 543). Separately, a crashed server's stale lock was taken over and its late save was refused, so newer data survived.
notes.recommendation: Check a session lock inside every UpdateAsync (refuse writes when the lock is not yours), let players start at once on a stand-in profile, block purchases until the real profile is open, and merge only earned currency and stats when it opens.
applies_when: A game saves currency or purchases per player
Players can rejoin quickly or be in two servers
limits: Tested on an in-memory DataStore stand-in in Studio, not Roblox's live DataStore
Lock timings (180 s stale, 20 s retry) are this game's choices, not measured optima

evidence.detail: Section 23: the planted-lock rejoin test and the automated stale-lock and refused-late-save tests.

notes.title: The nearest water to a creature inland can be across the island from its target
notes.observation: Island creatures hand a chase over to a sea form when the target enters the water. Spawning the sea form at the water nearest the island creature put it on the far side of the island (the creature stood in the island's middle), hundreds of studs from the target. Taking the water nearest a point stepped from the target back toward the creature instead put it 59 studs from the target, on the same side, within 0.2 s of the target entering the water.
notes.recommendation: When a handover spawns something near a creature to chase a target, search for the spawn point from the target's side (a point between target and creature), not from the creature's position.
applies_when: Handing an AI from one medium or zone to another (land to sea, inside to outside)
limits: Measured on one island with a boat starting just offshore

evidence.detail: Point 4 (jade frogs): entering 59 studs away on the thief's side after the fix.

notes.title: Test player-versus-player rules with a stand-in when only one client exists
notes.observation: A single-client Studio session cannot create a second Player. The catch, knockdown, immunity and close-range steal rules were still exercised on the server with the real goblin as victim and a stand-in table (a rig plus the few Player members the code uses) as the thief. It found the order and timing mistakes in the test, refused a steal on a standing target, a steal from too far, and a catch inside a protected zone.
notes.recommendation: Write server rules so they take the player objects as arguments, then drive them from a temporary test hook with a stand-in. State plainly in the report that replication, latency, prompts and real input were not covered.
applies_when: Adding a rule between two players
Only one client is available to test with
limits: A stand-in does not test replication, latency, client prompts or real input
A real two-client or multi-client session is still required before calling the feature multiplayer-ready

evidence.detail: Section 10 lists the stand-in thief tests and what they did not cover.

notes.title: Studio's Edit mode keeps old module code after a script is changed
notes.observation: A Luau test suite run in Studio's Edit mode (through Studio MCP's execute_luau) kept failing on a bug that had already been fixed and synced into the ModuleScript's Source: require returned the cached result of the old source. Replacing every game and test ModuleScript with a fresh Clone (same name and parent) before requiring made the next run use the new code, and the test passed.
notes.recommendation: Before re-running Edit-mode tests after changing a ModuleScript's Source, replace each changed ModuleScript with a fresh clone (or reopen the place), and treat a failure that matches already-fixed code as a cache symptom first.
applies_when: Running Luau tests or tools from Studio's command bar or Studio MCP in Edit mode
Syncing script sources into Studio without the Rojo plugin
limits: Observed in one Studio version in October 2026 through Studio MCP execute_luau
Play mode starts fresh VMs and was not affected

evidence.detail: GAME_DESIGN.md V11 lessons (2) and the report's section 22: the preset test failed after its fix was synced, then passed once the modules were replaced with clones.

notes.title: Studio MCP's simulated mouse leaves the camera Fixed
notes.observation: In a Studio play session, any Studio MCP user_mouse_input action (a plain x/y move as well as an instance_path click) switched workspace.CurrentCamera.CameraType from Custom to Fixed, and it stayed Fixed. When the game then teleported the character (raid start onto a flying ship, 5,000 studs away) the camera stayed behind at the old place, which looked exactly like a game bug. A listener on the camera's CameraType showed the change at the moment of the mouse action; no game code sets Fixed (searched), and setting Custom from a client execute_luau restored a following camera at once. The tool's x/y coordinates were also 58 px above the game's own mouse and viewport coordinates (the GUI inset).
notes.recommendation: After any simulated mouse action in a Studio playtest, reset the camera (CameraType = Custom) from a client execute_luau before judging what the camera shows, and log CameraType changes before reporting a camera bug. Convert WorldToViewportPoint y to the tool's coordinates by subtracting the GUI inset, or click buttons by instance_path.
applies_when: Playtesting a Roblox game through Studio MCP input tools
Judging camera behaviour, or anything after a teleport, in a session that used the simulated mouse
limits: One Windows PC, Studio in October 2026, a 1346 x 640 play viewport
Whether the tool restores the camera later on its own was not established; real mice are unaffected

evidence.detail: Section 12, last bullet; the camera log read '5.3:Custom ... 9.4:Fixed' around a simulated click, and 'Fixed' again after a plain x/y move.

notes.title: Studio screenshots arrive too late to catch short animations
notes.observation: Studio MCP screen captures arrived one to two seconds after the input that started a show, so repeated attempts missed 1 to 2 second spectacles (a toast flight, a satellite launch). The sequences were confirmed instead by client-reported events (toaster_chain_seen, gag_recovered), server state, and before/after screenshots.
notes.recommendation: For short animations, have the client report that the sequence ran and capture still before and after states; do not conclude an effect is broken from a capture that missed it.
applies_when: Verifying short visual effects through Studio MCP screenshots
limits: Timing observed on one Windows machine with one Studio version
A human watching the screen remains the real test of how a show feels

evidence.detail: The report's 'Not tested, and limits' section and Studio test 1 describe how shows were verified.

notes.title: Studio MCP's simulated keys do not trigger ProximityPrompts
notes.observation: In a Studio play session driven through Studio MCP, holding E with user_keyboard_input beside an enabled, in-range treasure prompt (9 studs of a 10-stud reach, no line-of-sight requirement) never triggered it, and calling InputHoldBegin/InputHoldEnd on the prompt from execute_luau in the client did not either: a server listener on Triggered and on ProximityPromptService saw nothing. The same session's simulated keys did reach the game's own UserInputService and ContextActionService handlers (H opened a card, R fired a boat ability, Backspace left spectating). Calling the server function the prompt calls, from a Studio-only test script, worked.
notes.recommendation: Do not count a prompt as untestable or broken because simulated keys cannot hold it. Test a prompt's effect through a Studio-only server test command that calls the same function, test the key path only where the game binds the key itself, and say in the report which prompts were not held by a key.
applies_when: Playtesting a Roblox game through Studio MCP input tools
A feature is reached by holding a ProximityPrompt
limits: One Windows PC, Studio in October 2026, keyboard input only
Real players' prompt input is unaffected; earlier Loot Goblins sessions reached prompts through the game's own reach-prompt fallback, which was not exercised here

evidence.detail: Sections 30 and 32: held E and InputHoldBegin never reached the server; the steal worked through a test command calling Loot.tryGrab.

notes.title: Edit-mode Luau tests can load sources straight from disk over a loopback file server
notes.observation: The team's launcher opened Studio on a freshly built game place that did not contain the test folder, and connecting the Rojo plugin needs clicks in Studio's UI. Instead, a Python `http.server` bound to 127.0.0.1 served the test and source folders, and a Studio MCP execute_luau call in Edit mode set HttpService.HttpEnabled to true, fetched each file with GetAsync into a new ModuleScript (fresh instances, so no cached require ran), and set HttpEnabled back to its old value in the same call. GetAsync failed with 'HTTP requests are not enabled' until the setting was toggled. Comparing each fetched source with the existing ModuleScript's Source also proved which modules in the open place differed from disk (two did, both just renamed); the full suite then ran from the files on disk.
notes.recommendation: To run Edit-mode tests from the files on disk without the Rojo plugin: serve the folders on 127.0.0.1 only, toggle HttpEnabled inside the same execute_luau call and restore it there (even on error, with pcall), replace modules with fresh instances rather than editing Source, report which sources differed, and stop the file server afterwards.
applies_when: Running a Luau test suite in Studio's Edit mode through Studio MCP
The open place lacks the test folder or may be out of date with the repository
limits: One Windows machine, one Studio version and Studio MCP's execute_luau in October 2026
The toggled setting belongs to the open place; only do this in a disposable built place that nobody will save over real work

evidence.detail: Section 6: every shared and server module replaced with a fresh copy fetched from disk; only the two renamed files differed; 140 of 140 Luau tests passed.

notes.title: Test reaching an objective through its intended route
notes.observation: The V6 report records Ninety finding that the Skull Chalice ladder was blocked. The geometry dated from V2, while intervening tests teleported to the objective and missed the route failure.
notes.recommendation: Include a normal-movement journey from the intended starting point to interaction and return. Teleports can isolate a mechanic but cannot establish route accessibility.
applies_when: Testing objectives reached through ladders, doors, terrain, stairs, or vehicles
limits: This observation does not establish that other routes are broken
The reported repair was walked in a single-client Studio test; broad multiplayer acceptance remains separate

evidence.detail: Section 13, issue 14 attributes the finding to Ninety; the repair was tested on foot from the pier to the chalice.

notes.title: Check a carved terrain space by reading the terrain, not the script
notes.observation: A volcano's crater was meant to be hollowed by a stack of air fills 2.2 studs thick. In a Studio test an air fill thinner than one 4-stud terrain cell removed nothing, so the summit was solid and the treasure inside it unreachable from the first version that had it. A raycast through the crater centre hit the summit; a thick air block cleared it.
notes.recommendation: Make carving fills at least one terrain cell (4 studs) thick, then verify the result by reading voxels or raycasting through the space before calling it reachable. A path-finding query from the approach to the objective is a quick follow-up, not a substitute for walking it.
applies_when: Generating terrain by script
A treasure or route sits inside a carved cave, crater or tunnel
limits: Observed in one Studio build with Terrain:FillCylinder; other fill shapes were not compared
The measured threshold is this game's observation, not an engine specification

evidence.detail: Section 18 records the crater centre reading 129.8 before the fix and 113.1 after, and a path from the beach reaching the crown.
